title: Bernardo O'Higgins's birth chart
metaDescription: Bernardo O'Higgins's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.6° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 27.6° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 27.6° Leo: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mars. A fire sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 20.1° Virgo, Venus at 5.5° Libra, Mars at 4.8° Leo. Mercury in an earth sign reads as a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; Venus in an air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Venus a sixth of the circle apart from Mars, 0.8° off exact. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Mercury square Uranus at 0.9°, and Neptune trine Pluto at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Leo at 27.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Virgo at 20.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 5.5° is in domicile; Jupiter in Virgo at 5.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 earth, 2 fire, 2 air, 1 water by element and 4 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by mode. Pluto crossed from Aquarius into Capricorn during that day, so its sign is left open. Pluto was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.3° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
